slides.title: Solve this in ==15 seconds== — most pick the trap

slides.stem: If x² = 49, what is the sum of all solutions to the equation?
slides.prompt: Time yourself. Comment your time and your answer.

slides.title: A — 0
slides.body: x² = 49 has two solutions: 7 and −7. Their sum is 0. Picking 7 means you found one root and stopped — squaring erases the sign, so the negative root is always hiding.

slides.title: Even powers hide negative roots
slides.body: Whenever the variable is squared, ask for both roots before you answer — x² = k has two solutions for any positive k, because (−7)² is just as much 49 as 7² is. The SAT writes "sum of all solutions" precisely to catch the students who stop at one.
